bug_semantics: CIPster's generic AttributeInsert(CipDataType, void*) binds an untyped storage cookie to an arbitrary CIP type with no layout check. An API-enabled deployment can register the same ByteBuf object as both a writable kCipByteArray and a writable kCipUdint. A remote unauthenticated EtherNet/IP SetAttributeSingle on the UDINT view hits DecodeData(kCipUdint), which stores 32 bits into ByteBuf.start (the first pointer of {start, limit}) while leaving limit unchanged, inflating logical size. A following GetAttributeSingle or SetAttributeSingle on the byte-array view hits EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray), which construct BufReader/BufWriter from that poisoned ByteBuf; BufWriter::append then memcpy's against attacker-controlled start/limit (ASan: 80-byte OOB read/write from backing-16). The default sample is not claimed exploitable; the primitive is CIPster's public attribute-registration API plus generic Get/SetAttrData.
flaw_origin: 90721b00e44e461d14501bb20714a4d71d9e18e4 (2018-07-24, Dick Hollenbeck) first replaced struct CipByteArray {EipUint16 length; EipByte* data} with class ByteBuf {start, limit} as the kCipByteArray backing object and rewrote EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray) to copy via BufReader/BufWriter constructed from that ByteBuf (cipcommon.cc: BufWriter w = *(ByteBuf*) data; w.append(aBuf)). Parent d06f16ea2ef9a10b894324a80ec686443708ed59 still memcpy'd cip_byte_array->data for cip_byte_array->length; class ByteBuf and the *(ByteBuf*) casts are absent there. git log -L on the DecodeData kCipByteArray case at the affected commit shows those lines originate in 90721b0 with no later edit through e8e9dba. Untyped AttributeInsert auto-binding SetAttrData already existed (e21ae61); 90721b0 is the first write of this advisory's ByteBuf.start / BufWriter::append mechanism. 90721b0 is a mixed encapsulation commit but the surviving first-write of those lines; no finer public member is reconstructable. The 2026 fix did not change append; it typed AttributeInsert and added an overlap guard.

reasoning: CVE-2026-13592 is a real, published VulDB/NVD record (not withdrawn). The first-party issue demonstrates a two-stage remote OOB write: untyped AttributeInsert aliases one ByteBuf as kCipByteArray and kCipUdint; SetAttributeSingle on the UDINT view poisons ByteBuf.start; EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray) then feed that ByteBuf to BufWriter::append, whose bounds check is against the poisoned view. Vulnerability-first BIC search used git log -L on the affected DecodeData(kCipByteArray) lines and -S for class ByteBuf / *(ByteBuf*) rather than scanning for AI markers. Those lines and class ByteBuf first appear in 90721b00e44e461d14501bb20714a4d71d9e18e4; they are absent at immediate parent d06f16ea2ef9a10b894324a80ec686443708ed59, which still used CipByteArray {length, data} and memcpy of length bytes. 90721b0 is a mixed encapsulation commit, but it is the smallest surviving public first-write of this start/limit codec (single parent, no reconstructable member commits, clone has only master). Earlier untyped insertAttribute/AttributeInsert and SetAttrData are preconditions and/or moves/refactors, not this variant's first-write; 3ca83ee moved the void* overload and is not a BIC. Tag membership is N/A (rolling, no tags); BIC precedes e8e9dba and the repro SHA, and the named patch 3a0159e lands after that ceiling on master. AI judgment is BIC-only: 90721b0 is human-authored by Dick Hollenbeck in 2018 with no commit-object AI marker. Claude co-authorship on the 2026 fix does not attribute the introducer. Verdict NOT_AI.
